The priest shall examine it, and if it appears to be beneath the skin and the hair in it has turned white, the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection that has broken out in the boil. (13:20).
But when the priest examines it, if there is no white hair in it, and it is not beneath the skin and has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days. (13:21).
If it spreads any further on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is an infection. (13:22).
But if the spot remains unchanged and does not spread, it is only the scar from the boil, and the priest shall pronounce him clean. (13:23).
When there is a burn on someone’s skin and the raw area of the burn becomes reddish-white or white, (13:24).

the priest must examine it. If the hair in the spot has turned white and the spot appears to be deeper than the skin, it is a disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection. (13:25).
But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in the spot, and it is not beneath the skin but has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days. (13:26).
On the seventh day the priest is to reexamine him, and if it has spread further on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection. (13:27).
But if the spot is unchanged and has not spread on the skin but has faded, it is a swelling from the burn, and the priest is to pronounce him clean; for it is only the scar from the burn. (13:28).
If a man or woman has an infection on the head or chin, (13:29).

the priest shall examine the infection, and if it appears to be deeper than the skin and the hair in it is yellow and thin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a scaly outbreak, an infectious disease of the head or chin. (13:30).

But if the priest examines the scaly infection and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, the priest shall isolate the infected person for seven days. (13:31).
On the seventh day the priest is to reexamine the infection, and if the scaly outbreak has not spread and there is no yellow hair in it, and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin, (13:32).
then the person must shave himself except for the scaly area. Then the priest shall isolate him for another seven days. (13:33).

On the seventh day the priest shall examine the scaly outbreak, and if it has not spread on the skin and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, the priest is to pronounce him clean. He must wash his clothes, and he will be clean. (13:34).
If, however, the scaly outbreak spreads further on the skin after his cleansing, (13:35).
the priest is to examine him, and if the scaly outbreak has spread on the skin, the priest need not look for yellow hair; the person is unclean. (13:36).
If, however, in his sight the scaly outbreak is unchanged and black hair has grown in it, then it has healed. He is clean, and the priest is to pronounce him clean. (13:37).
When a man or a woman has white spots on the skin, (13:38).
the priest shall examine them, and if the spots are dull white, it is a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin; the person is clean. (13:39).
Now if a man loses his hair and is bald, he is still clean. (13:40).
Or if his hairline recedes and he is bald on his forehead, he is still clean. (13:41).
But if there is a reddish-white sore on the bald head or forehead, it is an infectious disease breaking out on it. (13:42).
The priest is to examine him, and if the swelling of the infection on his bald head or forehead is reddish-white like a skin disease, (13:43).
the man is diseased; he is unclean. The priest must pronounce him unclean because of the infection on his head. (13:44).
A diseased person must wear torn clothes and let his hair hang loose, and he must cover his mouth and cry out, ‘Unclean, unclean!’ (13:45).
As long as he has the infection, he remains unclean. He must live alone in a place outside the camp. (13:46).
If any fabric is contaminated with mildew— any wool or linen garment, (13:47).
any weave or knit of linen or wool, or any article of leather— (13:48).
and if the mark in the fabric, leather, weave, knit, or leather article is green or red, then it is contaminated with mildew and must be shown to the priest. (13:49).
And the priest is to examine the mildew and isolate the contaminated fabric for seven days. (13:50).

On the seventh day the priest shall reexamine it, and if the mildew has spread in the fabric, weave, knit, or leather, then regardless of how it is used, it is a harmful mildew; the article is unclean. (13:51).
He is to burn the fabric, weave, or knit, whether the contaminated item is wool or linen or leather. Since the mildew is harmful, the article must be burned up. (13:52).
But when the priest reexamines it, if the mildew has not spread in the fabric, weave, knit, or leather article, (13:53).
the priest is to order the contaminated article to be washed and isolated for another seven days. (13:54).

After it has been washed, the priest is to reexamine it, and if the mildewed article has not changed in appearance, it is unclean. Even though the mildew has not spread, you must burn it, whether the rot is on the front or back. (13:55).
If the priest examines it and the mildew has faded after it has been washed, he must cut the contaminated section out of the fabric, leather, weave, or knit. (13:56).
But if it reappears in the fabric, weave, or knit, or on any leather article, it is spreading. You must burn the contaminated article. (13:57).
If the mildew disappears from the fabric, weave, or knit, or any leather article after washing, then it is to be washed again, and it will be clean. (13:58).
This is the law concerning a mildew contamination in wool or linen fabric, weave, or knit, or any leather article, for pronouncing it clean or unclean.” (13:59).
crossRefs: Leviticus 14:1-32: What happens after the priest finds the affliction healed.
Numbers 12:9-15: Miriam is struck and shut outside the camp for seven days.
2 Kings 5:1-14: Naaman the Aramean commander washes seven times in the Jordan and his flesh is restored.
2 Chronicles 26:19-21: King Uzziah is struck in the temple and lives in a separate house until his death.
Luke 17:11-14: Ten men stand at a distance, and Jesus sends them to show themselves to the priests.

translationNotes.note: Not the disease known today as leprosy, which is Hansen's disease and is caused by a bacterium identified in 1873. Tsaraat covers a range of surface conditions, and the same word is applied to marks in wool, linen and leather (13:47-59) and to growths in the plaster of a house (14:34-53), which no human illness does. The priest's job in this chapter is not to treat anything; it is to look, measure, wait seven days, look again, and rule the person clean or unclean.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: וְרָאָהוּ הַכֹּהֵן (ve-raahu ha-kohen), 'and the priest shall look at him'
translationNotes.note: This chapter is a diagnostic procedure, not a treatment. The priest looks for three signs, depth below the skin, whitened hair, and spread, then isolates the person for seven days and looks again, and can isolate for a second seven (13:4-6). No medicine is prescribed anywhere in it.

translationNotes.term: covered head to foot is clean
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כֻּלּוֹ הָפַךְ לָבָן (kullo hafakh lavan), 'it has all turned white'
translationNotes.note: Leviticus 13:12-13 rules that if the condition covers the whole body the man is clean, while a patch of raw flesh makes him unclean again (13:14). The verdict runs opposite to what a modern reader expects. What the chapter is tracking is the state of the condition, not the amount of it.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בְּגָדָיו יִהְיוּ פְרֻמִים (begadav yihyu ferumim)
translationNotes.note: The signs of mourning, worn by the living. Leviticus 13:45 requires torn clothes, unbound hair, a covered upper lip, and the cry 'Unclean, unclean,' so that others can keep their distance. Leviticus 10:6 forbids the same mourning signs to priests on duty.

The same word covers marks in wool, linen, and leather here (13:47-59) and in the plaster and stones of a house in Leviticus 14:33-53. No human illness spreads to a garment or a wall, which is why tsaraat cannot be read as one disease. The text treats it as a single category of contamination in people, cloth, and buildings.

stories.keyTakeaway: Moses and Aaron receive instructions on how priests are to examine and pronounce judgment on various skin diseases and moldy fabrics, using observation of depth, hair color, and spread to determine cleanness or uncleanness. Those with defiling diseases must wear torn clothes, keep their hair unkempt, cover their face, and live outside the camp.

stories.title: 🚫 Leviticus 14
summaryBullets: Then the LORD said to Moses, (14:1).
“This is the law for the one afflicted with a skin disease on the day of his cleansing, when he is brought to the priest. (14:2).
The priest is to go outside the camp to examine him, and if the skin disease of the afflicted person has healed, (14:3).
the priest shall order that two live clean birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop be brought for the one to be cleansed. (14:4).
Then the priest shall command that one of the birds be slaughtered over fresh water in a clay pot. (14:5).
And he is to take the live bird together with the cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop, and dip them into the blood of the bird that was slaughtered over the fresh water. (14:6).
Seven times he shall sprinkle the one to be cleansed of the skin disease. Then he shall pronounce him clean and release the live bird into the open field. (14:7).

The one being cleansed must wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and bathe with water; then he will be ceremonially clean. Afterward, he may enter the camp, but he must remain outside his tent for seven days. (14:8).
On the seventh day he must shave off all his hair — his head, his beard, his eyebrows, and the rest of his hair. He must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water, and he will be clean. (14:9).

On the eighth day he is to bring two unblemished male lambs, an unblemished ewe lamb a year old, a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with olive oil, and one log of olive oil. (14:10).
The priest who performs the cleansing shall present the one to be cleansed, together with these offerings, before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. (14:11).
Then the priest is to take one of the male lambs and present it as a guilt offering, along with the log of olive oil; and he must wave them as a wave offering before the LORD. (14:12).

Then he is to slaughter the lamb in the sanctuary area where the sin offering and burnt offering are slaughtered. Like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the priest; it is most holy. (14:13).

The priest is to take some of the blood from the guilt offering and put it on the right earlobe of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot. (14:14).
Then the priest shall take some of the log of olive oil, pour it into his left palm, (14:15).
dip his right forefinger into the oil in his left palm, and sprinkle some of the oil with his finger seven times before the LORD. (14:16).

And the priest is to put some of the oil remaining in his palm on the right earlobe of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on top of the blood of the guilt offering. (14:17).
The rest of the oil in his palm, the priest is to put on the head of the one to be cleansed, to make atonement for him before the LORD. (14:18).
Then the priest is to sacrifice the sin offering and make atonement for the one to be cleansed from his uncleanness. After that, the priest shall slaughter the burnt offering (14:19).
and offer it on the altar, with the grain offering, to make atonement for him, and he will be clean. (14:20).

If, however, the person is poor and cannot afford these offerings, he is to take one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved to make atonement for him, along with a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with olive oil for a grain offering, a log of olive oil, (14:21).
and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford, one to be a sin offering and the other a burnt offering. (14:22).
On the eighth day he is to bring them for his cleansing to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting before the LORD. (14:23).
The priest shall take the lamb for the guilt offering, along with the log of olive oil, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD. (14:24).

And after he slaughters the lamb for the guilt offering, the priest is to take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the right earlobe of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot. (14:25).
Then the priest is to pour some of the oil into his left palm (14:26).
and sprinkle with his right forefinger some of the oil in his left palm seven times before the LORD. (14:27).

The priest shall also put some of the oil in his palm on the right earlobe of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot — on the same places as the blood of the guilt offering. (14:28).
The rest of the oil in his palm, the priest is to put on the head of the one to be cleansed, to make atonement for him before the LORD. (14:29).
Then he must sacrifice the turtledoves or young pigeons, whichever he can afford, (14:30).
one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, together with the grain offering. In this way the priest will make atonement before the LORD for the one to be cleansed. (14:31).
This is the law for someone who has a skin disease and cannot afford the cost of his cleansing.” (14:32).
Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, (14:33).
“When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as your possession, and I put a contamination of mildew into a house in that land, (14:34).
the owner of the house shall come and tell the priest, ‘Something like mildew has appeared in my house.’ (14:35).

The priest must order that the house be cleared before he enters it to examine the mildew, so that nothing in the house will become unclean. After this, the priest shall go in to inspect the house. (14:36).
He is to examine the house, and if the mildew on the walls consists of green or red depressions that appear to be beneath the surface of the wall, (14:37).
the priest shall go outside the doorway of the house and close it up for seven days. (14:38).
On the seventh day the priest is to return and inspect the house. If the mildew has spread on the walls, (14:39).
he must order that the contaminated stones be pulled out and thrown into an unclean place outside the city. (14:40).
And he shall have the inside of the house scraped completely and the plaster that is scraped off dumped into an unclean place outside the city. (14:41).
So different stones must be obtained to replace the contaminated ones, as well as additional mortar to replaster the house. (14:42).
If the mildew reappears in the house after the stones have been torn out and the house has been scraped and replastered, (14:43).
the priest must come and inspect it. If the mildew has spread in the house, it is a destructive mildew; the house is unclean. (14:44).
It must be torn down with its stones, its timbers, and all its plaster, and taken outside the city to an unclean place. (14:45).
Anyone who enters the house during any of the days that it is closed up will be unclean until evening. (14:46).
And anyone who sleeps in the house or eats in it must wash his clothes. (14:47).
If, however, the priest comes and inspects it, and the mildew has not spread after the house has been replastered, he shall pronounce the house clean, because the mildew is gone. (14:48).
He is to take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop to purify the house; (14:49).
and he shall slaughter one of the birds over fresh water in a clay pot. (14:50).
Then he shall take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet yarn, and the live bird, dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times. (14:51).
And he shall cleanse the house with the bird’s blood, the fresh water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the scarlet yarn. (14:52).
Finally, he is to release the live bird into the open fields outside the city. In this way he will make atonement for the house, and it will be clean. (14:53).
This is the law for any infectious skin disease, for a scaly outbreak, (14:54).
for mildew in clothing or in a house, (14:55).
and for a swelling, rash, or spot, (14:56).
to determine when something is clean or unclean. This is the law regarding skin diseases and mildew.” (14:57).
crossRefs: Leviticus 13:1-46: The examination that has to come first, and the verdict this chapter reverses.
Matthew 8:2-4: Jesus tells the cleansed man to show himself to the priest and offer what Moses commanded.
Mark 1:40-45: The same command given, and the man spreading the news instead.
Numbers 19:6: Cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet wool thrown into the fire with the red heifer.
Psalm 51:7: Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צָרַעַת (ṣāraʿat), Greek: λέπρα (lepra), Aramaic: ܨܪܥܬܐ (ṣaraʿta)
translationNotes.note: A range of skin conditions, mildew, or mold; not limited to Hansen’s disease. Could affect people, garments, or houses.
The standard Old Testament dry measure for grain, about 22 quarts or 5.8 gallons (22 liters). Ruth carries home an ephah of barley after a day's gleaning (Ruth 2:17).

A small, fragrant herb (Origanum syriacum / Syrian oregano), growing in rocky soil. Bunches of hyssop were used to apply Passover blood to the doorposts (Exodus 12:22), in leper-cleansing rituals (Leviticus 14:6), and held up to Jesus on the cross with a wine-soaked sponge (John 19:29).

translationNotes.term: two birds, cedar, scarlet, and hyssop
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֵץ אֶרֶז וּשְׁנִי תוֹלַעַת וְאֵזֹב (ets erez u-sheni tolaat ve-ezov)
translationNotes.note: One bird is killed over fresh water in a clay pot and the second is dipped in its blood and released alive (14:5-7). The same four items, cedar, scarlet wool, hyssop, and a slaughtered animal, appear again at the red heifer in Numbers 19:6. Hyssop is the small brush; cedar and scarlet are the durable and the vivid.

The smallest liquid measure named in the Hebrew Bible, one twelfth of a hin, roughly a third of a liter or about ten fluid ounces. It appears only in Leviticus 14, where a single log of olive oil is used for the cleansing rite (14:10, 14:12, 14:21).

About 6.6 liters of fine flour, roughly seven quarts, for the full version of the offering. Leviticus 14:21 cuts it to one tenth, about 2.2 liters, and swaps two lambs for two birds if the man is poor. The cleansing is the same either way; only the price changes.

stories.keyTakeaway: God gives Moses procedures for cleansing people healed of skin diseases, including rituals with birds, oil, and animal offerings, with a simpler alternative for those who cannot afford the standard sacrifices. Instructions are also given for examining houses with spreading mold, tearing them down if the mold persists, and purifying them with bird blood if the mold is gone.

stories.title: 🚫 Leviticus 15
summaryBullets: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, (15:1).
“Say to the Israelites, ‘When any man has a bodily discharge, the discharge is unclean. (15:2).
This uncleanness is from his discharge, whether his body allows the discharge to flow or blocks it. So his discharge will bring about uncleanness. (15:3).
Any bed on which the man with the discharge lies will be unclean, and any furniture on which he sits will be unclean. (15:4).
Anyone who touches his bed must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening. (15:5).
Whoever sits on furniture on which the man with the discharge was sitting must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening. (15:6).
Whoever touches the body of the man with a discharge must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening. (15:7).
If the man with the discharge spits on one who is clean, that person must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening. (15:8).
Any saddle on which the man with the discharge rides will be unclean. (15:9).
Whoever touches anything that was under him will be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such things must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening. (15:10).

If the man with the discharge touches anyone without first rinsing his hands with water, the one who was touched must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening. (15:11).
Any clay pot that the man with the discharge touches must be broken, and any wooden utensil must be rinsed with water. (15:12).
When the man has been cleansed from his discharge, he must count off seven days for his cleansing, wash his clothes, and bathe himself in fresh water, and he shall be clean. (15:13).
On the eighth day he is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, come before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, and give them to the priest. (15:14).
The priest is to sacrifice them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for the man before the LORD because of his discharge. (15:15).
When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body with water, and he will be unclean until evening. (15:16).
Any clothing or leather on which there is an emission of semen must be washed with water, and it will remain unclean until evening. (15:17).
If a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both must bathe with water, and they will remain unclean until evening. (15:18).
When a woman has a discharge consisting of blood from her body, she will be unclean due to her menstruation for seven days, and anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening. (15:19).
Anything on which she lies or sits during her menstruation will be unclean, (15:20).
and anyone who touches her bed must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening. (15:21).
Whoever touches any furniture on which she was sitting must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening. (15:22).
And whether it is a bed or furniture on which she was sitting, whoever touches it will be unclean until evening. (15:23).
If a man lies with her and her menstrual flow touches him, he will be unclean for seven days, and any bed on which he lies will become unclean. (15:24).

When a woman has a discharge of her blood for many days at a time other than her menstrual period, or if it continues beyond her period, she will be unclean all the days of her unclean discharge, just as she is during the days of her menstruation. (15:25).
Any bed on which she lies or any furniture on which she sits during the days of her discharge will be unclean, like her bed during her menstrual period. (15:26).
Anyone who touches these things will be unclean; he must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening. (15:27).
When a woman is cleansed of her discharge, she must count off seven days, and after that she will be ceremonially clean. (15:28).
On the eighth day she is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. (15:29).
The priest is to sacrifice one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for her before the LORD for her unclean discharge. (15:30).
You must keep the children of Israel separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die by defiling My tabernacle, which is among them. (15:31).
This is the law of him who has a discharge, of the man who has an emission of semen whereby he is unclean, (15:32).
of a woman in her menstrual period, of any male or female who has a discharge, and of a man who lies with an unclean woman.’” (15:33).
crossRefs: Leviticus 12:1-8: The related law for a woman after childbirth, closing with the same offering.
Numbers 5:1-4: Anyone with a discharge or a skin disease is sent outside the camp.
Leviticus 22:4-7: A priest with a discharge may not eat the sacred offerings until sunset and a washing.
Mark 5:25-34: A woman with a flow of blood for twelve years reaches through the crowd to touch His cloak.
2 Samuel 11:4: Bathsheba is described as purifying herself from her uncleanness.

translationNotes.note: A general term for an abnormal bodily flow, not a named disease. The chapter distinguishes it from ordinary emissions and from menstruation, and prescribes washing, waiting until evening, and for the chronic case a seven-day count and two birds (15:13-15). Mark 5:25 describes a woman under exactly this chapter's long-term condition.

The most common ruling in the chapter, and the one that shows the scale of the system: most uncleanness ended at sundown with a wash. The Hebrew day turns at evening, so the status lapsed the same night. Leviticus 22:6-7 applies the same limit to priests.

translationNotes.term: lest they die by defiling My tabernacle
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: וְלֹא יָמֻתוּ בְּטֻמְאָתָם (ve-lo yamutu betumatam)
translationNotes.note: Leviticus 15:31 gives the reason for the whole chapter: the danger is uncleanness carried into the sanctuary, not uncleanness itself. Numbers 5:1-4 acts on the same principle by moving affected people outside the camp while the tent stands in the middle of it.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מִשְׁכָּב (mishkav), a bed - מוֹשָׁב (moshav), a seat
translationNotes.note: The rules at 15:4-12 and 15:19-27 work outward by contact: the bed, the seat, the saddle, anyone who touches them, anyone the man spits on, and any clay pot he handles, which is broken. The remedy in almost every case is the same and it is small, wash your clothes, bathe, and be clean at sunset. What the chapter builds is a traceable chain of contact, not a scale of guilt.

translationNotes.term: a discharge of blood for many days
translationNotes.note: Verses 15:25-30 cover bleeding outside the monthly cycle or continuing past it, and rule the woman unclean for as long as it lasts, with everything she lies or sits on unclean too. That is the standing of the woman in Matthew 9:20-22, Mark 5:25-34 and Luke 8:43-48, who had bled for twelve years: twelve years in which touching anyone passed the uncleanness on, which is why she comes up behind Him and says nothing.

stories.keyTakeaway: The LORD establishes rules for various bodily discharges; anyone or anything touched by someone with a discharge becomes unclean and requires washing and waiting until evening, with purification offerings required after seven days of cleansing.

stories.title: 🐐 Leviticus 16
summaryBullets: Now the LORD spoke to Moses after the death of two of Aaron’s sons when they approached the presence of the LORD. (16:1).

And the LORD said to Moses: “Tell your brother Aaron not to enter freely into the Most Holy Place behind the veil in front of the mercy seat on the ark, or else he will die, because I appear in the cloud above the mercy seat. (16:2).
This is how Aaron is to enter the Holy Place: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering. (16:3).

He is to wear the sacred linen tunic, with linen undergarments. He must tie a linen sash around him and put on the linen turban. These are holy garments, and he must bathe himself with water before he wears them. (16:4).
And he shall take from the congregation of Israel two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering. (16:5).
Aaron is to present the bull for his sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household. (16:6).
Then he shall take the two goats and present them before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. (16:7).
After Aaron casts lots for the two goats, one for the LORD and the other for the scapegoat, (16:8).
he shall present the goat chosen by lot for the LORD and sacrifice it as a sin offering. (16:9).
But the goat chosen by lot as the scapegoat shall be presented alive before the LORD to make atonement by sending it into the wilderness as the scapegoat. (16:10).
When Aaron presents the bull for his sin offering and makes atonement for himself and his household, he is to slaughter the bull for his own sin offering. (16:11).
Then he must take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD, and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense, and take them inside the veil. (16:12).
He is to put the incense on the fire before the LORD, and the cloud of incense will cover the mercy seat above the Testimony, so that he will not die. (16:13).

And he is to take some of the bull’s blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the east side of the mercy seat; then he shall sprinkle some of it with his finger seven times before the mercy seat. (16:14).

Aaron shall then slaughter the goat for the sin offering for the people and bring its blood behind the veil, and with its blood he must do as he did with the bull’s blood: He is to sprinkle it against the mercy seat and in front of it. (16:15).

So he shall make atonement for the Most Holy Place because of the impurities and rebellious acts of the Israelites in regard to all their sins. He is to do the same for the Tent of Meeting which abides among them in the midst of their impurities. (16:16).

No one may be in the Tent of Meeting from the time Aaron goes in to make atonement in the Most Holy Place until he leaves, after he has made atonement for himself, his household, and the whole assembly of Israel. (16:17).

Then he shall go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it. He is to take some of the bull’s blood and some of the goat’s blood and put it on all the horns of the altar. (16:18).
He is to sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times to cleanse it and consecrate it from the uncleanness of the Israelites. (16:19).
When Aaron has finished purifying the Most Holy Place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, he is to bring forward the live goat. (16:20).

Then he is to lay both hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities and rebellious acts of the Israelites in regard to all their sins. He is to put them on the goat’s head and send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a man appointed for the task. (16:21).
The goat will carry on itself all their iniquities into a solitary place, and the man will release it into the wilderness. (16:22).
Then Aaron is to enter the Tent of Meeting, take off the linen garments he put on before entering the Most Holy Place, and leave them there. (16:23).

He is to bathe himself with water in a holy place and put on his own clothes. Then he must go out and sacrifice his burnt offering and the people’s burnt offering to make atonement for himself and for the people. (16:24).
He is also to burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar. (16:25).
The man who released the goat as the scapegoat must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water; afterward he may reenter the camp. (16:26).

The bull for the sin offering and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought into the Most Holy Place to make atonement, must be taken outside the camp; and their hides, flesh, and dung must be burned up. (16:27).
The one who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water, and afterward he may reenter the camp. (16:28).

This is to be a permanent statute for you: On the tenth day of the seventh month, you shall humble yourselves and not do any work — whether the native or the foreigner who resides among you — (16:29).
because on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you, and you will be clean from all your sins before the LORD. (16:30).
It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, that you may humble yourselves; it is a permanent statute. (16:31).
The priest who is anointed and ordained to succeed his father as high priest shall make atonement. He will put on the sacred linen garments (16:32).
and make atonement for the Most Holy Place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, and for the priests and all the people of the assembly. (16:33).
This is to be a permanent statute for you, to make atonement once a year for the Israelites because of all their sins.” And all this was done as the LORD had commanded Moses. (16:34).
crossRefs: Hebrews 9:7: The high priest enters the Holy Place once a year, not without blood.
Hebrews 9:12: Christ entered once for all with His own blood, securing eternal redemption.
Leviticus 23:26-32: Further instructions about the Day of Atonement fasting.
Numbers 29:7-11: Sacrificial details for the Day of Atonement.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כִּפֶּר (kipper), to cover or wipe clean - יוֹם הַכִּפֻּרִים (Yom ha-Kippurim)
translationNotes.note: This chapter is where the word does its heaviest work: atonement is made for the Most Holy Place, for the tent, for the altar, for the priests and for the whole assembly (16:16-20, 16:33). The order is fixed, the sanctuary first and the people last, because the book treats accumulated uncleanness as something that settles on the building. Verse 16:30 states the day's purpose in one line, that on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you from all your sins.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֲזָאזֵל (ʿazāʾzel), Greek: ἀποπομπαῖος τράγος (apopompaíos tragos), Aramaic: עזאזל (azazel)
translationNotes.note: Goat sent away into the wilderness carrying Israel’s sins; some interpret the name as a place, a demon, or simply 'complete removal.'

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים (qōdesh haqqodāšim), Greek: ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων (hagia tōn hagiōn), Aramaic: קודשא דקודשיא (qudsha d-qudsha)
translationNotes.note: The inner sanctuary where the ark and mercy seat were kept; entered only once a year by the high priest.

The seventh day, set apart by God's command (Exodus 20:8-11). All work ceased from sunset Friday to sunset Saturday. By Jesus' day, rabbinical tradition had elaborated 39 categories of forbidden labor; many of Jesus' healings deliberately challenged those additional rules without violating the Torah command itself.

The tenth day of the seventh month (16:29), the one day of the year the high priest went behind the veil, and the only fast the law of Moses commands. Leviticus 23:27-32 repeats the date and makes it a Sabbath of complete rest running evening to evening. Numbers 29:7-11 gives the offerings for the day.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תְּעַנּוּ אֶת־נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם (teannu et-nafshoteikhem), 'you shall afflict your souls'
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew says afflict the soul, and Israel has always kept it as a fast; Isaiah 58:3-5 argues about fasting using this same verb, and Acts 27:9 calls the season simply 'the Fast.' Leviticus never spells out the method, only the requirement.

On this one day the high priest laid aside the gold, the ephod, and the breastpiece, bathed, and put on plain linen (16:4). He changed back into his own garments only after the goat had been sent away (16:23-24). The most important service of the year was done in the simplest dress he owned.

Two goats stand at the tent entrance and lots decide which is which (16:8). No one chooses. The pair are treated as one sin offering for the people (16:5): one dies and its blood is carried inside, the other carries the confessed sins away alive into the wilderness.

stories.keyTakeaway: The Day of Atonement is established with the high priest entering the Most Holy Place once a year with sacrifices, cleansing blood rites, and the scapegoat carrying sins into the wilderness.

stories.title: ⚖️ Leviticus 17
summaryBullets: Then the LORD said to Moses, (17:1).
“Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites and tell them this is what the LORD has commanded: (17:2).
‘Anyone from the house of Israel who slaughters an ox, a lamb, or a goat in the camp or outside of it (17:3).

instead of bringing it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD before His tabernacle— that man shall incur bloodguilt. He has shed blood and must be cut off from among his people. (17:4).

For this reason the Israelites will bring to the LORD the sacrifices they have been offering in the open fields. They are to bring them to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and offer them as sacrifices of peace offerings to the LORD. (17:5).
The priest will then splatter the blood on the altar of the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. (17:6).
They must no longer offer their sacrifices to the goat demons to which they have prostituted themselves. This will be a permanent statute for them for the generations to come.’ (17:7).
Tell them that if anyone from the house of Israel or any foreigner living among them offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice (17:8).
but does not bring it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting to sacrifice it to the LORD, that man must be cut off from his people. (17:9).
If anyone from the house of Israel or a foreigner living among them eats any blood, I will set My face against that person and cut him off from among his people. (17:10).
For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you to make atonement for your souls upon the altar; for it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul. (17:11).
Therefore I say to the Israelites, ‘None of you may eat blood, nor may any foreigner living among you eat blood.’ (17:12).
And if any Israelite or foreigner living among them hunts down a wild animal or bird that may be eaten, he must drain its blood and cover it with dirt. (17:13).

For the life of all flesh is its blood. Therefore I have told the Israelites, ‘You must not eat the blood of any living thing, because the life of all flesh is its blood; whoever eats it must be cut off.’ (17:14).

And any person, whether native or foreigner, who eats anything found dead or mauled by wild beasts must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening; then he will be clean. (17:15).
But if he does not wash his clothes and bathe himself, then he shall bear his iniquity.” (17:16).
crossRefs: Genesis 9:4-6: Flesh with its lifeblood still in it is not to be eaten.
Deuteronomy 12:20-25: Once in the land, meat may be slaughtered anywhere, but the blood must be poured out on the ground.
Acts 15:19-20: Gentile believers are told to abstain from blood and from what has been strangled.
2 Chronicles 11:15: Jeroboam appoints his own priests for the high places and for the goat idols.
Hebrews 9:22: Without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כִּפֶּר (kipper) - נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh), life or living being
translationNotes.note: Leviticus 17:11 is the sentence the whole sacrificial system rests on: the life of the flesh is in the blood, and God has given it on the altar to make atonement, because it is the blood that makes atonement by the life. That is the stated reason for the ban on eating blood in the same verse. Hebrews 9:22 restates the principle, that without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כָּרֵת (karet), to be cut off
translationNotes.note: A fixed legal formula, used four times in this chapter alone (17:4, 17:9, 17:10, 17:14). It removes a person from the covenant community and its protections; the text does not say whether a court carries it out or God does, and it names no human executioner. Genesis 17:14 applies it to a man who is not circumcised, and Exodus 30:33 and 30:38 to anyone who copies the sanctuary's anointing oil or incense for private use.

The same word means a he-goat, and it is used here for what Israel had been sacrificing to in the open fields (17:7). 2 Chronicles 11:15 records Jeroboam appointing priests for the high places and for these seirim. Isaiah 13:21 and 34:14 place them in ruins and wasteland.

translationNotes.term: the life is in the blood
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נֶפֶשׁ הַבָּשָׂר בַּדָּם (nefesh ha-basar ba-dam)
translationNotes.note: Nefesh is the word for a life or a living self, so the sentence says the life of the creature is in its blood. Leviticus 17:11 gives this as the reason blood is not eaten and the reason it works on the altar. Genesis 9:4 states the same rule to Noah, long before Sinai.

translationNotes.term: drain its blood and cover it
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: וְכִסָּהוּ בֶּעָפָר (ve-khissahu be-afar), 'and cover it with dust'
translationNotes.note: Game killed in the hunt cannot be brought to the altar, so its blood is poured out and buried in the ground (17:13). Deuteronomy 12:16 and 12:24 give the same instruction for animals slaughtered for meat once Israel is spread across the land.

The verb is the ordinary word for a woman selling herself, and Leviticus 17:7 aims it at Israel sacrificing to the goat demons. Scripture uses it for false worship from Exodus 34:15-16 onward, and the whole book of Hosea is built on it. English translations that read 'were unfaithful' are accurate but drop the deliberate harshness of the Hebrew.

Leviticus 17:4 charges the man who kills an ox, lamb, or goat away from the Tent with bloodguilt, the same legal category the law uses for murder. In the ancient Near East every slaughter of a domestic animal was a religious act performed at a shrine, so a household killing its own beast in the open field was in practice worshipping somewhere. The law does not ban meat; it bans the private altar.

stories.keyTakeaway: God commands all sacrifices be brought to the tent of meeting rather than offered in the fields or to goat idols, and strictly forbids eating blood since it represents life and makes atonement; anyone violating these rules will be cut off from the people.

stories.title: ⚖️ Leviticus 18
summaryBullets: Then the LORD said to Moses, (18:1).
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: I am the LORD your God. (18:2).

You must not follow the practices of the land of Egypt, where you used to live, and you must not follow the practices of the land of Canaan, into which I am bringing you. You must not walk in their customs. (18:3).
You are to practice My judgments and keep My statutes by walking in them. I am the LORD your God. (18:4).
Keep My statutes and My judgments, for the man who does these things will live by them. I am the LORD. (18:5).
None of you are to approach any close relative to have sexual relations. I am the LORD. (18:6).
You must not expose the nakedness of your father by having sexual relations with your mother. She is your mother; you must not have sexual relations with her. (18:7).
You must not have sexual relations with your father’s wife; it would dishonor your father. (18:8).
You must not have sexual relations with your sister, either your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter, whether she was born in the same home or elsewhere. (18:9).
You must not have sexual relations with your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter, for that would shame your family. (18:10).
You must not have sexual relations with the daughter of your father’s wife, born to your father; she is your sister. (18:11).
You must not have sexual relations with your father’s sister; she is your father’s close relative. (18:12).
You must not have sexual relations with your mother’s sister, for she is your mother’s close relative. (18:13).
You must not dishonor your father’s brother by approaching his wife to have sexual relations with her; she is your aunt. (18:14).
You must not have sexual relations with your daughter-in-law. She is your son’s wife; you are not to have sexual relations with her. (18:15).
You must not have sexual relations with your brother’s wife; that would shame your brother. (18:16).

You must not have sexual relations with both a woman and her daughter. You are not to marry her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter and have sexual relations with her. They are close relatives; it is depraved. (18:17).
You must not take your wife’s sister as a rival wife and have sexual relations with her while your wife is still alive. (18:18).
You must not approach a woman to have sexual relations with her during her menstrual period. (18:19).
You must not lie carnally with your neighbor’s wife and thus defile yourself with her. (18:20).
You must not give any of your children to be sacrificed to Molech, for you must not profane the name of your God. I am the LORD. (18:21).
You must not lie with a man as with a woman; that is an abomination. (18:22).
You must not lie carnally with any animal, thus defiling yourself with it; a woman must not stand before an animal to mate with it; that is a perversion. (18:23).
Do not defile yourselves by any of these practices, for by all these things the nations I am driving out before you have defiled themselves. (18:24).
Even the land has become defiled, so I am punishing it for its sin, and the land will vomit out its inhabitants. (18:25).
But you are to keep My statutes and ordinances, and you must not commit any of these abominations— neither your native-born nor the foreigner who lives among you. (18:26).
For the men who were in the land before you committed all these abominations, and the land has become defiled. (18:27).
So if you defile the land, it will vomit you out as it spewed out the nations before you. (18:28).
Therefore anyone who commits any of these abominations must be cut off from among his people. (18:29).
You must keep My charge not to practice any of the abominable customs that were practiced before you, so that you do not defile yourselves by them. I am the LORD your God.” (18:30).
crossRefs: Leviticus 20:10-21: The same prohibitions listed again, this time with the penalties attached.
Deuteronomy 27:20-23: Curses pronounced at Mount Ebal on these same relations.
Deuteronomy 25:5-6: Levirate marriage, the one case in which a man takes his dead brother's widow.
Genesis 19:30-38: Lot's daughters, and the origin of Moab and Ammon.
1 Corinthians 5:1-5: A man in Corinth has his father's wife, a thing not found even among the nations.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: טָמֵא (ṭāmēʾ), Greek: μιαίνω (miainō), Aramaic: ܛܢܦ (ṭanap)
translationNotes.note: To make ritually or morally polluted; used for blood, sexual sin, idolatry, and necromancy.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כָּרֵת (karēt), Greek: ἐξολοθρεύω (exolothreuō), Aramaic: כרת (karat)
translationNotes.note: To be removed from the people, sometimes by death, sometimes by exclusion; the text does not always specify which.

A fixed legal idiom for sexual relations, used through Leviticus 18 and 20 and nowhere meaning merely to see someone undressed. Modern versions replace it with plain wording, which is clearer but hides that the chapter is using one consistent formula for every case it lists.

translationNotes.term: the land will vomit you out
translationNotes.note: A deliberately physical verb, used of the land three times in this book (18:25, 18:28, 20:22) and of the fish in Jonah 2:10. The land is treated as party to the covenant, capable of being defiled and of expelling those who defile it.

translationNotes.term: the practices of Egypt and Canaan
translationNotes.note: Leviticus 18:3 frames the chapter between the country Israel had just left and the country it was entering. Deuteronomy 18:9-12 lists the Canaanite practices in the same terms. The command is not to a people in isolation but to one moving from one culture into another.

translationNotes.term: Molech and what the sacrifice was
translationNotes.note: Leviticus 18:21 forbids giving a child to Molech, and Scripture says elsewhere exactly what that meant: burning sons and daughters in the fire (Deuteronomy 12:31, Jeremiah 7:31), or making them pass through the fire (2 Kings 23:10). Two kings of Judah did it to their own sons, Ahaz in 2 Kings 16:3 and Manasseh in 2 Kings 21:6. Diodorus Siculus, writing in the first century BC about Carthage in 310 BC, describes a bronze image of the god with hands sloping downward so that a child laid on them rolled into a pit of fire beneath. Carthage was a Phoenician colony, and its sacrificial precinct has yielded thousands of urns holding the burned bones of infants.

translationNotes.term: the Valley of Hinnom, later called Gehenna
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גֵּיא בֶן־הִנֹּם (Ge Ben-Hinnom) - Greek: γέεννα (geenna)
translationNotes.note: The child sacrifice had an address. It was carried out at the Topheth in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, the ravine running along the south and west sides of Jerusalem, which is why Jeremiah 7:31 and 32:35 and 2 Kings 23:10 all name the same ground. The Hebrew name of that valley came into Greek as Gehenna. That word appears twelve times in the New Testament and is translated hell; eleven of the twelve are spoken by Jesus, at Matthew 5:22 and 5:29-30, 10:28, 18:9, 23:15 and 23:33, Mark 9:43-47, and Luke 12:5.

Leviticus 18:3 tells Israel not to walk in the customs of Canaan, and the reader is expected to know what those were. Excavations at Ras Shamra on the Syrian coast, ancient Ugarit, begun in 1929 under Claude Schaeffer, recovered clay tablets that name the same gods Scripture names: El, Baal the storm god, Asherah, and Anat. Their worship centered on rain, herds, and fertility, and it was worked out at open-air platforms, standing stones, and wooden poles, which is why the law keeps attacking those three objects.

translationNotes.term: You shall not lie with a male
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: וְאֶת־זָכָר לֹא תִשְׁכַּב מִשְׁכְּבֵי אִשָּׁה (ve-et zakhar lo tishkav mishkevei ishah) - תּוֹעֵבָה (to'evah)
translationNotes.note: Zakhar is the plain Hebrew word for a male, used of male animals and male children as well as men. Mishkevei ishah is literally 'the lyings of a woman,' the chapter's idiom for the sexual act, so 18:22 reads word for word 'and with a male you shall not lie the lyings of a woman.' To'evah, which English renders abomination or detestable thing, is the term this chapter attaches to the practices it lists, and the Greek Old Testament renders it bdelygma. Leviticus 20:13 states the same prohibition and adds the penalty.

translationNotes.term: Where Paul's word arsenokoitai comes from
translationNotes.original: Greek (LXX) Leviticus 18:22: μετὰ ἄρσενος οὐ κοιμηθήσῃ κοίτην γυναικός - Greek (LXX) Leviticus 20:13: ὃς ἂν κοιμηθῇ μετὰ ἄρσενος κοίτην γυναικός - Greek: ἀρσενοκοῖται (arsenokoitai), singular ἀρσενοκοίτης (arsenokoites)
translationNotes.note: Paul's word arsenokoitai, at 1 Corinthians 6:9 and 1 Timothy 1:10, means men who lie with males. Literally it is male-bedders: men who engage in sexual acts with other males. Koite is the ordinary Greek word for a bed and the standard term for sexual intercourse, which is how the New Testament itself uses it at Romans 13:13 and Hebrews 13:4. The word is a rare compound, and its two halves stand side by side in the Greek Old Testament of these two verses: Leviticus 18:22 reads meta arsenos ou koimethese koiten gynaikos, and Leviticus 20:13 reads hos an koimethe meta arsenos koiten gynaikos, where arsenos and koiten are adjacent.

stories.keyTakeaway: God forbids the Israelites from sexual relations with close relatives, with animals, with a neighbor's wife, during menstruation, and from sacrificing children to Molek; those who practice these things will be cut off from their people.

stories.title: ⚖️ Leviticus 19
summaryBullets: Then the LORD said to Moses, (19:1).
“Speak to the whole congregation of Israel and tell them: Be holy because I, the LORD your God, am holy. (19:2).
Each of you must respect his mother and father, and you must keep My Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God. (19:3).
Do not turn to idols or make for yourselves molten gods. I am the LORD your God. (19:4).
When you sacrifice a peace offering to the LORD, you shall offer it for your acceptance. (19:5).
It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it, or on the next day; but what remains on the third day must be burned up. (19:6).
If any of it is eaten on the third day, it is tainted and will not be accepted. (19:7).
Whoever eats it will bear his iniquity, for he has profaned what is holy to the LORD. That person must be cut off from his people. (19:8).
When you reap the harvest of your land, you are not to reap to the very edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest. (19:9).
You must not strip your vineyard bare or gather its fallen grapes. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God. (19:10).
You must not steal. You must not lie or deceive one another. (19:11).
You must not swear falsely by My name and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD. (19:12).
You must not defraud your neighbor or rob him. You must not withhold until morning the wages due a hired hand. (19:13).
You must not curse the deaf or place a stumbling block before the blind, but you shall fear your God. I am the LORD. (19:14).
You must not pervert justice; you must not show partiality to the poor or favoritism to the rich; you are to judge your neighbor fairly. (19:15).
You must not go about spreading slander among your people. You must not endanger the life of your neighbor. I am the LORD. (19:16).
You must not harbor hatred against your brother in your heart. Directly rebuke your neighbor, so that you will not incur guilt on account of him. (19:17).
Do not seek revenge or bear a grudge against any of your people, but love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD. (19:18).

You are to keep My statutes. You shall not crossbreed two different kinds of livestock; you shall not sow your fields with two kinds of seed; and you shall not wear clothing made of two kinds of material. (19:19).

If a man lies carnally with a slave girl promised to another man but who has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there must be due punishment. But they are not to be put to death, because she had not been freed. (19:20).
The man, however, must bring a ram to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting as his guilt offering to the LORD. (19:21).
The priest shall make atonement on his behalf before the LORD with the ram of the guilt offering for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven the sin he has committed. (19:22).
When you enter the land and plant any kind of tree for food, you shall regard the fruit as forbidden. For three years it will be forbidden to you and must not be eaten. (19:23).
In the fourth year all its fruit must be consecrated as a praise offering to the LORD. (19:24).
But in the fifth year you may eat its fruit; thus your harvest will be increased. I am the LORD your God. (19:25).
You must not eat anything with blood still in it. You must not practice divination or sorcery. (19:26).
You must not cut off the hair at the sides of your head or clip off the edges of your beard. (19:27).
You must not make any cuts in your bodies for the dead or put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the LORD. (19:28).
You must not defile your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will be prostituted and filled with depravity. (19:29).
You must keep My Sabbaths and have reverence for My sanctuary. I am the LORD. (19:30).
You must not turn to mediums or spiritists; do not seek them out, or you will be defiled by them. I am the LORD your God. (19:31).
You are to rise in the presence of the elderly, honor the aged, and fear your God. I am the LORD. (19:32).
When a foreigner resides with you in your land, you must not oppress him. (19:33).
You must treat the foreigner living among you as native-born and love him as yourself, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God. (19:34).
You must not use dishonest measures of length, weight, or volume. (19:35).
You shall maintain honest scales and weights, an honest ephah, and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. (19:36).
You must keep all My statutes and all My ordinances and follow them. I am the LORD.” (19:37).
crossRefs: Matthew 22:39: Jesus names love your neighbor as yourself as the second great commandment.
Ruth 2:2-9: Ruth gleans behind the harvesters in Boaz's field under the right this chapter grants.
Deuteronomy 24:19-22: The forgotten sheaf, the olive branch, and the fallen grapes left for the poor.
Deuteronomy 25:13-16: Do not carry two differing weights in your bag or keep two differing measures in your house.
James 5:4: The wages you failed to pay the workmen are crying out against you.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אוֹב (ʾov) / יִדְּעֹנִי (yiddeʿoni), Greek: ἐγγαστρίμυθος (engastrimythos) / μάντις (mantis), Aramaic: אובא (ʾova) / ידעונא (yidʿona)
translationNotes.note: Spiritist or consulter of the dead; strictly forbidden under penalty of death.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כָּרֵת (karēt), Greek: ἐξολοθρεύω (exolothreuō), Aramaic: כרת (karat)
translationNotes.note: To be removed from the people, sometimes by death, sometimes by exclusion; the text does not always specify which.
The standard Old Testament dry measure for grain, about 22 quarts or 5.8 gallons (22 liters). Ruth carries home an ephah of barley after a day's gleaning (Ruth 2:17).
The standard temple liquid measure for wine and oil in offerings; about one gallon (3.8 liters). Used throughout Exodus and Numbers for prescribed drink offerings.

Three separate rights, each with its own Hebrew name: the standing edge of the field left uncut, the stalks dropped during reaping, and the grapes missed or fallen in the vineyard. Deuteronomy 24:19 adds a fourth, the forgotten sheaf. Ruth 2 shows the whole system working, and it is a right of the poor, not a gift of the owner.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לֹא־תָלִין פְּעֻלַּת שָׂכִיר (lo-talin peullat sakhir)
translationNotes.note: Day laborers were paid at the end of each day because they had nothing to live on until they were. Deuteronomy 24:14-15 spells out the reason: he is poor and is counting on it. James 5:4 charges rich landowners with exactly this offense.

Leviticus 19:19 forbids crossbreeding livestock, sowing a field with two kinds of seed, and wearing cloth of two kinds; Deuteronomy 22:11 identifies the cloth as wool and linen together and gives it the name shaatnez. The priestly garments of Exodus 28 are made of exactly that mixture, which reserved it for the sanctuary.

For three years the fruit of a newly planted tree is literally called uncircumcised, using the same noun as the foreskin of Genesis 17:11. In the fourth year the whole crop is holy, and only in the fifth may the owner eat it (19:23-25). English 'forbidden' loses the image entirely.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מֹאזְנֵי צֶדֶק אַבְנֵי־צֶדֶק (mozne tsedeq avne-tsedeq), 'scales of righteousness, stones of righteousness'
translationNotes.note: Weights were carved stones carried in a pouch, so a dishonest trader kept a heavy set for buying and a light set for selling; Deuteronomy 25:13 forbids exactly that. Inscribed stone shekel weights from Judah have been recovered by excavation in Jerusalem and elsewhere. Proverbs 11:1 calls a false balance an abomination to the LORD.

Leviticus 19:26 bans two named crafts that ancient courts paid for. Diviners read the future from the livers of sacrificed sheep, from the flight of birds, and from arrows shaken out of a quiver, which is what the king of Babylon does at Ezekiel 21:21, and from patterns in liquid poured into a cup, the practice attached to Joseph's silver cup at Genesis 44:5. Deuteronomy 18:10-11 gives the fullest list of the trades Israel was to have none of.

translationNotes.term: cutting the body and shaving for the dead
translationNotes.note: Gashing the skin and hacking off the hair and beard were standard mourning rites across Canaan and Syria, and they were also used to get a god's attention: the prophets of Baal cut themselves with knives and lances until the blood ran, at 1 Kings 18:28. Jeremiah 16:6, 41:5, and 47:5 report Israelites and their neighbors doing the same over the dead. Leviticus 19:27-28 and Deuteronomy 14:1 forbid it to Israel, and Leviticus 21:5 repeats the ban for priests.

This phrase occurs once in the whole Hebrew Bible, here at Leviticus 19:28, and it sits in the same sentence as cutting for the dead. In the ancient world a permanent mark burned or pricked into the skin identified a slave with his owner, a captive with his captor, or a devotee with the god of a particular temple. The ban belongs with the mourning and divination laws around it, not with a general rule about decoration.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קְדֵשָׁה (qedeshah), a woman set apart for a shrine
translationNotes.note: Leviticus 19:29 is not aimed at street trade but at a father putting his daughter into it, and the surrounding law shows why. Deuteronomy 23:17-18 forbids any son or daughter of Israel to serve as a shrine prostitute and refuses the money earned that way as an offering. The Hebrew term is built on the root for holy, so the woman was formally consecrated to a sanctuary. Hosea 4:14 charges the men of Israel with sacrificing alongside these women.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: וְאָהַבְתָּ לְרֵעֲךָ כָּמוֹךָ (ve-ahavta le-reakha kamokha)
translationNotes.note: The sentence sits at 19:18, at the end of a run of practical rules about not stealing, not lying, not slandering, and not bearing a grudge; the same verse opens by forbidding revenge and grudge-holding. Jesus names it the second great commandment at Matthew 22:39 and Mark 12:31, and Paul says the whole law is summed up in it at Galatians 5:14 and Romans 13:9. Verse 19:34 extends the identical wording to the resident foreigner, 'you shall love him as yourself,' with the reason that you were foreigners in Egypt.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חֵרֵשׁ (cheresh), a deaf man - עִוֵּר (ivver), a blind man - מִכְשֹׁל (mikhshol), a stumbling block
translationNotes.note: Leviticus 19:14 picks two people who cannot catch you doing it: the deaf man cannot hear the curse and the blind man cannot see the obstacle. That is the point of the pairing, and the verse closes not with a penalty but with 'you shall fear your God,' the formula this chapter attaches to offences no court could prove. Deuteronomy 27:18 puts a public curse on anyone who misleads a blind man on the road.

stories.keyTakeaway: The LORD commands Israel to be holy and gives Moses a collection of laws covering respect for parents and the Sabbath, proper treatment of the poor and hired workers, fair judgment, sexual conduct, dietary rules, and honoring the elderly and foreigners.

stories.title: ⚖️ Leviticus 20
summaryBullets: Then the LORD said to Moses, (20:1).
“Tell the Israelites, ‘Any Israelite or foreigner living in Israel who gives any of his children to Molech must be put to death. The people of the land are to stone him. (20:2).
And I will set My face against that man and cut him off from his people, because by giving his offspring to Molech, he has defiled My sanctuary and profaned My holy name. (20:3).
And if the people of the land ever hide their eyes and fail to put to death the man who gives one of his children to Molech, (20:4).
then I will set My face against that man and his family and cut off from among their people both him and all who follow him in prostituting themselves with Molech. (20:5).
Whoever turns to mediums or spiritists to prostitute himself with them, I will also set My face against that person and cut him off from his people. (20:6).
Consecrate yourselves, therefore, and be holy, because I am the LORD your God. (20:7).
And you shall keep My statutes and practice them. I am the LORD who sanctifies you. (20:8).
If anyone curses his father or mother, he must be put to death. He has cursed his father or mother; his blood shall be upon him. (20:9).
If a man commits adultery with another man’s wife— with the wife of his neighbor— both the adulterer and the adulteress must surely be put to death. (20:10).
If a man lies with his father’s wife, he has uncovered his father’s nakedness. Both must surely be put to death; their blood is upon them. (20:11).
If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both must surely be put to death. They have acted perversely; their blood is upon them. (20:12).
If a man lies with a man as with a woman, they have both committed an abomination. They must surely be put to death; their blood is upon them. (20:13).
If a man marries both a woman and her mother, it is depraved. Both he and they must be burned in the fire, so that there will be no depravity among you. (20:14).
If a man lies carnally with an animal, he must be put to death. And you are also to kill the animal. (20:15).
If a woman approaches any animal to mate with it, you must kill both the woman and the animal. They must surely be put to death; their blood is upon them. (20:16).

If a man marries his sister, whether the daughter of his father or of his mother, and they have sexual relations, it is a disgrace. They must be cut off in the sight of their people. He has uncovered the nakedness of his sister; he shall bear his iniquity. (20:17).

If a man lies with a menstruating woman and has sexual relations with her, he has exposed the source of her flow, and she has uncovered the source of her blood. Both of them must be cut off from among their people. (20:18).
You must not have sexual relations with the sister of your mother or your father, for it is exposing one’s own kin; both shall bear their iniquity. (20:19).
If a man lies with his uncle’s wife, he has uncovered the nakedness of his uncle. They will bear their sin; they shall die childless. (20:20).
If a man marries his brother’s wife, it is an act of impurity. He has uncovered the nakedness of his brother; they shall be childless. (20:21).
You are therefore to keep all My statutes and ordinances, so that the land where I am bringing you to live will not vomit you out. (20:22).
You must not follow the statutes of the nations I am driving out before you. Because they did all these things, I abhorred them. (20:23).

But I have told you that you will inherit their land, since I will give it to you as an inheritance — a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God, who has set you apart from the peoples. (20:24).

You are therefore to distinguish between clean and unclean animals and birds. Do not become contaminated by any animal or bird, or by anything that crawls on the ground; I have set these apart as unclean for you. (20:25).
You are to be holy to Me because I, the LORD, am holy, and I have set you apart from the nations to be My own. (20:26).
A man or a woman who is a medium or spiritist must surely be put to death. They shall be stoned; their blood is upon them.’” (20:27).
crossRefs: Leviticus 18:6-30: The same prohibitions set out without penalties attached.
Deuteronomy 18:9-14: The list of forbidden practices Israel is not to learn from the nations of Canaan.
2 Kings 23:10: Josiah defiles Topheth so no one can make a son or daughter pass through the fire to Molech.
Jeremiah 32:35: High places of Baal in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, where children were offered to Molech.
1 Samuel 28:7-14: Saul consults a medium at En-dor after having banned them from the land.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אוֹב (ʾov) / יִדְּעֹנִי (yiddeʿoni), Greek: ἐγγαστρίμυθος (engastrimythos) / μάντις (mantis), Aramaic: אובא (ʾova) / ידעונא (yidʿona)
translationNotes.note: Spiritist or consulter of the dead; strictly forbidden under penalty of death.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כָּרֵת (karēt), Greek: ἐξολοθρεύω (exolothreuō), Aramaic: כרת (karat)
translationNotes.note: To be removed from the people, sometimes by death, sometimes by exclusion; the text does not always specify which.

translationNotes.term: pass through the fire to Molech
translationNotes.note: Leviticus 20:2-5 sets the death penalty on giving a child to Molech and adds a second penalty for a community that looks the other way. 2 Kings 23:10 has Josiah wrecking the site in the Valley of Ben Hinnom to stop it, and Jeremiah 32:35 names the same place. The practice is treated as importable, not theoretical.

translationNotes.term: I will set My face against
translationNotes.note: A judicial formula, the opposite of the blessing in Numbers 6:25 where the LORD makes His face shine on a person. It appears at 17:10, 20:3, 20:5, and 20:6, always where the community itself might fail to act. Ezekiel 14:8 uses the same phrase.

A legal declaration that the executed person, not the court, bears responsibility for the death. It runs through Leviticus 20 as the closing formula on capital cases. 2 Samuel 1:16 and Matthew 27:25 both use the same idiom.

Leviticus 20:2 and 20:27 assign stoning, and Deuteronomy 17:5-7 gives the procedure. The condemned was taken outside the town gate, at least two witnesses were required, and those witnesses threw first, before the rest of the people, so that a false accuser had to kill with his own hands. Jesus points at that rule at John 8:7. Acts 7:58 shows the witnesses laying their cloaks at the feet of a young man named Saul so they could throw freely.

Leviticus 20:4-5 anticipates a community that hides its eyes rather than act, and Israel's own record shows it happening at the top. Ahaz sacrificed his son in the fire (2 Kings 16:3) and Manasseh did the same and added sorcery, divination, and mediums (2 Kings 21:6). Josiah finally wrecked the site itself, defiling the Topheth in the Valley of Ben Hinnom so no one could use it again (2 Kings 23:10).

translationNotes.term: If a man lies with a male
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁכַּב אֶת־זָכָר מִשְׁכְּבֵי אִשָּׁה (ve-ish asher yishkav et zakhar mishkevei ishah) - דְּמֵיהֶם בָּם (demeihem bam)
translationNotes.note: Leviticus 20:13 repeats the wording of 18:22 and adds the sentence: both are put to death, and the chapter's closing formula follows, 'their blood is upon them,' which places responsibility for the death on the condemned rather than on the court. Leviticus 20 is the penalty chapter for the practices listed in chapter 18, and it runs the same way through the other cases it takes up. The Greek Old Testament of this verse is the source of the compound Paul uses at 1 Corinthians 6:9 and 1 Timothy 1:10.

translationNotes.term: Where Paul's word arsenokoitai comes from
translationNotes.original: Greek (LXX) Leviticus 18:22: μετὰ ἄρσενος οὐ κοιμηθήσῃ κοίτην γυναικός - Greek (LXX) Leviticus 20:13: ὃς ἂν κοιμηθῇ μετὰ ἄρσενος κοίτην γυναικός - Greek: ἀρσενοκοῖται (arsenokoitai), singular ἀρσενοκοίτης (arsenokoites)
translationNotes.note: Paul's word arsenokoitai, at 1 Corinthians 6:9 and 1 Timothy 1:10, means men who lie with males. Literally it is male-bedders: men who engage in sexual acts with other males. Koite is the ordinary Greek word for a bed and the standard term for sexual intercourse, which is how the New Testament itself uses it at Romans 13:13 and Hebrews 13:4. The word is a rare compound, and its two halves stand side by side in the Greek Old Testament of these two verses: Leviticus 18:22 reads meta arsenos ou koimethese koiten gynaikos, and Leviticus 20:13 reads hos an koimethe meta arsenos koiten gynaikos, where arsenos and koiten are adjacent.

stories.keyTakeaway: God commands Moses to enforce death penalties for child sacrifice to Molek, consulting mediums, cursing parents, adultery, incest, bestiality, and certain sexual violations; Israel must keep these decrees and distinctions between clean and unclean to remain holy and avoid being rejected by the land.

stories.title: 👨‍⚖️ Leviticus 21
summaryBullets: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to Aaron’s sons, the priests, and tell them that a priest is not to defile himself for a dead person among his people, (21:1).
except for his immediate family — his mother, father, son, daughter, or brother, (21:2).
or his unmarried sister who is near to him, since she has no husband. (21:3).
He is not to defile himself for those related to him by marriage, and so profane himself. (21:4).
Priests must not make bald spots on their heads, shave off the edges of their beards, or make cuts in their bodies. (21:5).
They must be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God. Because they present to the LORD the food offerings, the food of their God, they must be holy. (21:6).
A priest must not marry a woman defiled by prostitution or divorced by her husband, for the priest is holy to his God. (21:7).
You are to regard him as holy, since he presents the food of your God. He shall be holy to you, because I the LORD am holy — I who set you apart. (21:8).
If a priest’s daughter defiles herself by prostituting herself, she profanes her father; she must be burned in the fire. (21:9).

The priest who is highest among his brothers, who has had the anointing oil poured on his head and has been ordained to wear the priestly garments, must not let his hair hang loose or tear his garments. (21:10).
He must not go near any dead body; he must not defile himself, even for his father or mother. (21:11).
He must not leave or desecrate the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him. I am the LORD. (21:12).
The woman he marries must be a virgin. (21:13).
He is not to marry a widow, a divorced woman, or one defiled by prostitution. He is to marry a virgin from his own people, (21:14).
so that he does not defile his offspring among his people, for I am the LORD who sanctifies him.” (21:15).
Then the LORD said to Moses, (21:16).
“Say to Aaron, ‘For the generations to come, none of your descendants who has a physical defect may approach to offer the food of his God. (21:17).
No man who has any defect may approach — no man who is blind, lame, disfigured, or deformed; (21:18).
no man who has a broken foot or hand, (21:19).
or who is a hunchback or dwarf, or who has an eye defect, a festering rash, scabs, or a crushed testicle. (21:20).
No descendant of Aaron the priest who has a defect shall approach to present the food offerings to the LORD. Since he has a defect, he is not to come near to offer the food of his God. (21:21).
He may eat the most holy food of his God as well as the holy food, (21:22).
but because he has a defect, he must not go near the veil or approach the altar, so as not to desecrate My sanctuaries. For I am the LORD who sanctifies them.’” (21:23).
Moses told this to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites. (21:24).
crossRefs: Ezekiel 44:20-25: The same rules on a priest's hair, his marriage, and his contact with the dead.
Numbers 6:6-8: A Nazirite may not go near a dead body, even for his own father or mother, the same separation this chapter puts on the priests.
Leviticus 10:6-7: Aaron and his surviving sons are forbidden to mourn or to leave the tent, the case that lies behind the mourning restrictions here.
Leviticus 22:17-25: The animal brought to the altar must be without defect too, so the standard in 21:16-23 is about what comes near the altar rather than about the man's worth.
Leviticus 19:14: The same law forbids cursing the deaf or putting a stumbling block before the blind, which is how this code treats the disabled generally.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חָלַל (ḥālal), Greek: βεβηλόω (bebēloō), Aramaic: חלל (ḥll)
translationNotes.note: To treat something holy as common or ordinary.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קָדַשׁ (qadash), Greek: ἁγιάζω (hagiazō), Aramaic: קדש (qdsh)
translationNotes.note: To set apart as holy; God sanctifies priests and offerings.

Olive oil mixed with specific spices (Exodus 30:22-25), used to consecrate priests, kings, and tabernacle furniture. The Hebrew word for an anointed one is mashiach; transliterated 'Messiah.' The Greek equivalent is christos.

Leviticus 21:18-20 lists twelve conditions that bar a descendant of Aaron from serving at the altar. The bar is on service, not on standing: verse 22 keeps his right to eat the holy food with his family. The same word governs the animals in Leviticus 22:20-25.

translationNotes.term: must not let his hair hang loose
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֶת־רֹאשׁוֹ לֹא יִפְרָע (et-rosho lo yifra)
translationNotes.note: The mourning customs of Leviticus 13:45 are forbidden to the high priest, even for his own father or mother (21:10-11). Leviticus 10:6 had already imposed this on Aaron the day his sons died. The office does not pause for private grief.

translationNotes.term: defile himself for a dead person
translationNotes.note: Numbers 19:11-16 makes a corpse the strongest and longest source of uncleanness in the law: seven days, with washing on the third day and the seventh, and it passes to everyone who enters the tent and to any open container in it. Touching a grave or a single human bone in a field carries the same seven days. Leviticus 21:1-4 therefore bars an ordinary priest from a dead body except for his mother, father, son, daughter, brother, or unmarried sister, and 21:11 bars the high priest even from those. Luke 10:31-32 puts a priest and a Levite on the Jerusalem road beside a man left half dead.

stories.keyTakeaway: God establishes rules for priests regarding mourning practices, marriage, and physical appearance, with stricter requirements for the high priest; he also forbids any descendant of Aaron with physical defects from serving at the altar, though they may eat the holy food.

stories.title: 👨‍⚖️ Leviticus 22
summaryBullets: Then the LORD said to Moses, (22:1).
“Tell Aaron and his sons to treat with respect the sacred offerings that the Israelites have consecrated to Me, so that they do not profane My holy name. I am the LORD. (22:2).

Tell them that for the generations to come, if any of their descendants in a state of uncleanness approaches the sacred offerings that the Israelites consecrate to the LORD, that person must be cut off from My presence. I am the LORD. (22:3).

If a descendant of Aaron has a skin disease or a discharge, he may not eat the sacred offerings until he is clean. Whoever touches anything defiled by a corpse or by a man who has an emission of semen, (22:4).
or whoever touches a crawling creature or a person that makes him unclean, whatever the uncleanness may be — (22:5).
the man who touches any of these will remain unclean until evening. He must not eat from the sacred offerings unless he has bathed himself with water. (22:6).
When the sun has set, he will become clean, and then he may eat from the sacred offerings, for they are his food. (22:7).
He must not eat anything found dead or torn by wild animals, which would make him unclean. I am the LORD. (22:8).
The priests must keep My charge, lest they bear the guilt and die because they profane it. I am the LORD who sanctifies them. (22:9).
No one outside a priest’s family may eat the sacred offering, nor may the guest of a priest or his hired hand eat it. (22:10).
But if a priest buys a slave with his own money, or if a slave is born in his household, that slave may eat his food. (22:11).
If the priest’s daughter is married to a man other than a priest, she is not to eat of the sacred contributions. (22:12).
But if a priest’s daughter with no children becomes widowed or divorced and returns to her father’s house, she may share her father’s food as in her youth. But no outsider may share it. (22:13).
